subject: Re: Sentinel transition economics — structured onramp proposal
messages:
From: Samir Bose <samir@dataplex.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@sentinel-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sentinel offer + transition ask

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Sentinel has put together a competitive replacement offer for the inference stack that the team is reviewing. Two quick items we wanted to surface and see if Redwood has flexibility:

- Upfront pilot credit: they’re offering a 3-month bridge credit equivalent to ~40% of our first-quarter spend (applied to invoices).
- Seat/throughput packaging: they’ve proposed a tiered package (base reserved capacity + burst tokens) that reduces our per-token carry for predictable workloads.

We like Redwood’s runtime performance, but the economics matter for our board timing. Can you share what an accelerated onramp credit would look like, and whether you can mirror the billing carveouts for a pilot-to-production path?

I’ve attached the offer summary they sent (sentinel_offer_summary.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samir Bose
Head of Platform Engineering
DataPlex (procurement lead for Sentinel evaluation)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Samir Bose <samir@dataplex.io>
Cc: Elena Rodriguez <elena@sentinel-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel offer + transition ask

Samir —

Appreciate the note and for sharing the Sentinel summary. Quick top-line from my side: we can be competitive on an onramp credit and structure a phased reserved+burst package similar to what you described, but I want to make sure we align on the parts that actually move the needle for your team (SLOs, data controls, and migration friction).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short runbook and a draft credit structure (attached: redwood_onramp_credit_calc.xlsx) that outlines a 90-day pilot credit and a staged reservation discount tied to go-live milestones.
2) If that looks sane, we’ll do a 30-minute alignment call with your infra and procurement folks to lock the MA/PO timing and any billing carveouts.
3) We can include an explicit rollback/eval window (30 days) so you have an escape path if integration costs exceed estimates.

High-level offers in the attached sheet: 30% pilot credit applied to invoices in month 1, then step-down credits over months 2–3; a one-time migration credit to offset egress and runbook hours; and a technical SLA appendix for throughput baselines.

Can you confirm who on your side will sign the PO and the timing you’re working toward? We can be prepared to compress approvals if needed.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Exec — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sentinel offer + transition ask — need signoff on concession structure

Team — forwarding Sentinel’s ask and my proposed onramp credit. Key asks from the customer: a 90-day pilot credit (~30% month-1, step-down month 2–3), a migration credit to cover egress and runbook hours, and a billing carveout that lets them apply credits to invoices quickly. They named Sentinel Systems as the alternative with a fairly aggressive short-term credit.

Questions for you:
- Connor — can we absorb a one-time migration credit of up to $45k against the first invoice while preserving margin targets?
- Marissa — if they compress to an April-ish go-live (customer timeline), what does a 6-month reserved package at a 10% discount + burst look like operationally?
- Soojin — do we need exec approval for the pilot credit size I’ve sketched in the attached sheet?

I’ve pasted the original external email below for context.

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the modeled credit structure — we reviewed it with procurement and infra. Sentinel will accept the proposed 30% month-1 pilot credit applied to invoices, the migration credit up to $45k, and the staged reserved package (6 months at 10% + burst).

Two small asks before we go to PO:
1) Add a short clause in the invoice that specifies credit application timing (applied to the first invoice after pilot sign-off).
2) Can you provide a short technical ramp checklist so our ops team can validate the throughput targets during the 30-day eval window?

We’ve attached a PO stub (sntl_po_stub.pdf) that procurement will use to kick off internal signatures once we confirm the clause and the ramp checklist.

If you can send the clause language and ramp checklist by tomorrow, we’ll route the PO. Happy to sign this week.

Best,
Elena Rodriguez
VP, Cloud Partnerships
Sentinel Systems
